title: Pocket — Send. Request. Get paid.
track: Track 2: Access and Distribution for MUSD/MEZO

slides.title: Bitcoin capital needs everyday uses.
slides.intro: Mezo lets Bitcoin holders borrow MUSD. New users still need a simple way to turn that money into a payment, a request or productive savings.

cards.title: Access
cards.body: Wallet setup and unfamiliar transaction steps make the first payment harder than it should be.

cards.title: Use
cards.body: Borrowed MUSD needs useful destinations: other people, merchants and Savings.

cards.title: Confidence
cards.body: Users need a clear recipient, amount and confirmation before trusting a money app.

slides.footer: Pocket brings Mezo's money into familiar payment flows.

slides.title: Pocket. Send. Request. Get paid.
slides.intro: A mobile web app with social sign-in and a Privy embedded wallet. Users keep MUSD in their own wallet and send directly to a username or address.

cards.title: Sign in
cards.body: X, Telegram or email. An embedded wallet is created and synced to a Pocket profile.

cards.title: Pay and request
cards.body: Resolve a recipient, review the amount and sign a direct MUSD transfer.

cards.title: Borrow and save
cards.body: Access Mezo Troves and the sMUSD Savings vault from the same wallet.

slides.footer: Track 2: Access and Distribution for MUSD/MEZO.

slides.title: One wallet. Four useful actions.
slides.intro: Pocket combines direct payments, merchant invoices, Mezo Borrow and Savings. The wallet signs each payment; the server independently verifies its receipt.

cards.title: 01 · Send / Request
cards.body: Direct transfers and payment-request records support everyday payments.

cards.title: 02 · Borrow
cards.body: Open, inspect, repay or close a BTC-backed Trove using protocol-specific calls.

cards.title: 03 · Save
cards.body: Deposit MUSD, withdraw and claim Savings yield from the embedded wallet.

slides.footer: Live at mpocket.tech · Merchant checkout, corrected Savings accounting and configured welcome campaign.

slides.title: Wallet to wallet, verified on Mezo.
slides.intro: Pocket's payment path is direct. Postgres stores profiles, requests and activity; an internal ledger does not authorize or fund the current transfer flow.

cards.title: User wallet
cards.body: The Privy embedded wallet holds the MUSD and signs the ERC-20 transfer.

cards.title: Mezo
cards.body: Mezo executes the transfer. Native BTC pays gas; receiving requires no recipient transaction.

cards.title: Pocket API
cards.body: The server verifies transaction identity and outcome before recording payment activity.

slides.footer: Legacy vault settlement is isolated from direct payments.

slides.title: Borrow, save and welcome new users.
slides.intro: Wave 1 feedback recognized the Trove and sMUSD integrations as deep and protocol-correct. The remediation corrects the Savings false-zero read and adds a welcome claim.

cards.title: Troves
cards.body: BTC collateral, MUSD borrowing, position health and user-authorized repay/close actions.

cards.title: sMUSD Savings
cards.body: Deposits, withdrawals and yield claims. Claimable interest includes global-index accrual.

cards.title: 200 MEZO welcome
cards.body: One testnet claim, locked for two weekly epochs as a user-owned veMEZO NFT. Campaign deployed and funded with 200 MEZO, enough for one claim.

slides.footer: Repay and claimYield live execution receipts still need collection.

slides.title: A merchant checkout gives MUSD a destination.
slides.intro: A merchant creates an invoice, shares a payment link or QR, and receives a direct MUSD transfer with verified confirmation. Checkout is implemented; independent merchant pilots remain to be established.

cards.title: A reason to acquire MUSD
cards.body: Customers need MUSD to pay a merchant, extending the product beyond transfers among existing holders.

cards.title: A reason to keep using it
cards.body: Merchants receive funds directly and can reuse the wallet for payments or Savings.

cards.title: Measure actual use
cards.body: Track independent paying wallets, settled invoices, repeat customers and merchant feedback.

slides.footer: Welcome rewards support onboarding; their claims alone do not prove new MUSD demand.

slides.title: Merchant fees that can cover sponsored gas.
slides.intro: Proposed monetization starts with a disclosed merchant-payment fee. Set pricing after pilot feedback and measured gas costs; no fee rate, revenue or profitability is claimed yet.

cards.title: Merchant payments
cards.body: A small fee on successful merchant transactions, shown before payment.

cards.title: Gas sponsorship
cards.body: Allocate part of the fee to BTC gas and operating costs. Validate the margin using real transactions.

cards.title: Future services
cards.body: Premium merchant tools can follow demonstrated demand. Ordinary P2P sends are not the initial fee target.

slides.footer: Commercial hypothesis to validate with genuine merchants.

slides.title: Strong integration. Next: proof of use.
slides.intro: Builder: greyw0rks · github.com/greyw0rks/musd-pocket. Merchant checkout and the funded welcome campaign are live. Successful user transactions and independent adoption remain to be demonstrated.

cards.title: Technical evidence
cards.body: Welcome deployment and funding receipts are recorded; a real-token/escrow claim simulation succeeds. Regression and contract checks pass. User welcome, repay and claimYield receipts remain pending.

cards.title: Adoption targets
cards.body: Recruit 10–20 external users and 2–3 merchant pilots. Aim for 20+ transfers and 5+ requests. These are planning targets, not achieved metrics.

cards.title: Next milestones
cards.body: Collect missing embedded-wallet receipts; recruit genuine merchant pilots and external users; record feedback and returning usage. Additional welcome claims need more MEZO inventory.

slides.footer: Track 2 · Pilot service fees are zero. No external traction or revenue claimed.
